text:
Lia (Support): Hey team, customer rwd-acme reported a sudden spike of 429s starting ~11:03 UTC. They say it coincides with a nightly batch that switched to a 32k context payload. Can we triage?

Alex W: Do we have request IDs or sample headers? 429s could be per-model RPM/TMP or concurrency caps.

Lia (Support): I asked for logs, they sent a sample request id: req_0a9f3c. Header shows: Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>, Model: rwd-extended-32k-v1, Content-Length: 32768, x-client-version: acme-batcher/2.1.

Samir P: rwd-extended-32k-v1 has a lower RPM/TMP and tighter max_concurrency due to memory. If a big batch started, queueing + prefix cache could push active concurrency above per-instance cap -> 429 response from fronting layer.

Ben J: Posting recent quota table excerpt (sanitized):
```
model: rwd-extended-32k-v1
per_min_rpm: 300
per_min_tpm: 12000
max_concurrency_per_key: 6
context_limit_tokens: 32768
```

Maria G: Important: TPM refers to tokens-per-minute. Their batch increases tokens per request a lot so TPM can be exhausted fast even at low qps. 429s in this scenario usually show as "rate_limit_exceeded" in the API body. Any API error body?

Lia (Support): They pasted the error payload: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"model rwd-extended-32k-v1 token quota exceeded"}. They also saw intermittent 401 earlier this week but not now.

Alex W: That error string confirms token quota. Two likely causes: (A) global per-model TPM window saturated by larger contexts, or (B) token-burst guard triggered per API key. Need repro steps from customer and a short internal repro with an API key we control.

Samir P: I can simulate with a small script to send repeated 32k-context requests to that model. Lia, can you ask customer what their QPS was during the window? Also whether they were using streaming or non-streaming.

Lia (Support): They said burst launched at 11:02:47 UTC, single-threaded process that kicked off ~60 parallel requests over ~30s (their batch orchestrator spawns multiple workers). Not streaming, standard generate endpoint.

Ben J: 60 parallel * 32k tokens each = huge immediate token demand. If per-minute TPM is 12k tokens (example above) they'd overshoot immediately. Even if max_concurrency is 6, fronting will let some requests queue, but token accounting happens at acceptance, so early requests might be accepted then subsequent ones rejected once TPM window fills.

Alex W: For repro, try this curl (using our test key). Replace <API_KEY> and point to our staging model: rwd-extended-32k-v1-staging.

```
for i in {1..12}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-extended-32k-v1-staging","input":"'$(head -c 32000 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '\n')'"}' &
done
wait
```

Samir P: I'll run that against staging from my laptop in 5m and watch quota metrics. If I see 429s with similar error body, we can confirm TPM exhaustion. Also check for 429 subtype in headers: x-rwd-limit-type: token_tpm or concurrency.

Lia (Support): Customer also asked why they didn't see graceful queuing instead of immediate 429s. They expected requests to be queued up to their concurrency cap.

Ben J: Our fronting layer has both concurrency and token budget checks. For large contexts, token budget check happens at acceptance time because we need token count to bill and enforce TPM. That can cause immediate 429s even if queue slots exist. We do have a feature flag for request backlog queuing for certain tiers, but not enabled for this customer's plan.

Maria G: Also note we throttle long-context models more aggressively to protect cluster mem pressure. For example we cap max_concurrency_per_key to a lower number for 64k/32k models. If they were migrated from a smaller context model recently, their row-level cap might not have been adjusted — I'll verify.

eng-sre-oncall: tagging in. @eng-sre-oncall, can you look at cluster metrics around 2025-11-03T11:02:30Z-11:06:00Z for pool "mem-64k-east-1"? We want per-instance queue depth, kernel OOMs, and token-metering deltas.

eng-sre-oncall: On it. Pulling logs. One quick note: we saw a transient auth spike earlier (multiple 401s) from the same customer yesterday when they rotated keys. That could have caused them to retry in a tight loop, compounding token usage.

Samir P: Repro run in staging done. Observed pattern: first ~6 requests accepted, subsequent requests returned 429 after ~2s with body "rate_limit_exceeded token_tpm". Headers included x-rwd-remaining-tokens: 0 and x-rwd-reset-after: 54.

Ben J: Good repro. That header confirms TPM window exhaustion. Lia, relay back: to mitigate they can (1) reduce batch parallelism, (2) use smaller contexts where possible, (3) request dedicated capacity or increased TPM commit for this model via support plan.

Lia (Support): Customer asked for temporary workaround: is there a rate-limit bucket increase we can apply for a short window while they run nightly job?

Alex W: We can grant a short-term TPM bump but it requires approvals from infra-ops and billing. I can provision a 60-minute uplift to TPM for their API key in staging; for prod it needs a ticket to Sales for dedicated commit or support-approved bump.

eng-sre-oncall: FYI I saw a single instance that briefly hit GPU OOM and restarted at 11:04:10 — likely due to those large simultaneous 32k allocations. No persistent crashloop, but it explains some extra latency.

Maria G: Action items: (1) Lia to ask customer for exact batch size, QPS, and whether they'll accept scheduled throttling. (2) Samir to add test case to our load harness to simulate 32k burst patterns. (3) Alex to start TPM uplift approval conversation with infra-ops and Billing. (4) eng-sre-oncall to keep an eye on mem-64k-east-1 and set short alert if instance OOM rate > 1 in 5m.

Lia (Support): Noted. Lia -> customer: "We're seeing TPM exhaustion due to 32k contexts and parallelism. Short-term options: drop parallelism to <=6, stagger your batch, or request a time-limited TPM uplift while we coordinate a long-term plan (dedicated capacity)."

Customer follow-up (pasted): "We can stagger but that slows nightly job a lot. We'll take temporary uplift if you can. Also we saw a 401 yesterday during key rotation and retried automatically — we will add jitter. Thanks!" :thumbsup:

Ben J: For documentation, we'll add an FAQ entry: "Why do I get 429s when switching to extended contexts?" explaining TPM vs concurrency and showing examples of how to calculate token budget (tokens_per_request * QPS). Samir, can you draft?

Samir P: Yep will draft and post to docs/devex. Also adding internal runbook snippet to identify token_tpm vs concurrency 429s via response headers and body. Example header-> x-rwd-limit-type which helps triage.

Alex W: I'll queue the internal ticket for a 60-minute TPM uplift for customer rwd-acme, pending billing approval. Lia, I'll loop you in.

Lia (Support): Thanks all. Closing loop after uplift decision. Will also recommend they enable exponential backoff and add jitter when they retry on 401/429.

Ops Bot: Note created: #INC-1973102467 - "rwd-acme 429 spike during 32k batch" assigned to infra-ops.

Lia (Support): Marking resolved for now pending uplift. If eng-sre sees further OOMs I'll reopen. :white_check_mark:
